articles.resume: EUROPEAN SESSION In the European session, the main highlight was the UK Retail Sales report. The data showed a strong rebound in October, beating expectations across both headline and underlying measures, with volumes rising 0.7% m/m and sales excluding autos and fuel increasing 0.9%. The recovery was broad-based, supported by stronger food and non-food sales, while online spending also continued to expand. Although the figures point to resilient consumer demand, the three-month growth rate remained relatively modest at 0.4%. articles.titre: US approved nearly 900,000 Nvidia and AMD AI chips for China. Raises more questions than answers.
articles.resume: The disclosure adds to political pressure for tighter China chip rules, a risk for Nvidia and AMD’s China revenue at a time when AI and semiconductor shares are already being sold hard across Asia. Nvidia saying it has stopped H200 shipments limits the near-term earnings hit, but any formal tightening would also weigh on Chinese AI developers’ access to computing power. Hong Kong-listed Tencent, Alibaba and Baidu are the most exposed names on the Chinese side.
